svg.title: Binary Heap & Heapsort
svg.desc: Binary Heap & Heapsort. A complete binary tree packed into an array keeps the smallest item on top: O(log n) push and pop, the classic priority queue. Step 1, A tree in an array: Each parent ≤ its children, so the minimum is on top; filled level by level, it fits an array. Step 2, Push: sift up: push(3): append at index 7, swap up while smaller than the parent: past 7 and 4, stop under 1. Step 3, Pop: sift down: pop() returns 1; the last item, 7, takes the root and sinks past the smaller child: 2, then 6. Step 4, Heapsort and uses: Popping until empty yields 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 9: heapsort, O(n log n) even in the worst case.

g.text: Each parent ≤ its children, so the minimum is on top; filled level by level, it fits an array.
push(3): append at index 7, swap up while smaller than the parent: past 7 and 4, stop under 1.
pop() returns 1; the last item, 7, takes the root and sinks past the smaller child: 2, then 6.
Popping until empty yields 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 9: heapsort, O(n log n) even in the worst case.
so the smallest item is always the root.
Shape: complete, filled level by level,
so it packs into an array: no pointers.
Append at the next free slot, index 7.
Returns 1; the last item, 7, takes the root.
O(log n): at most one swap per level
n pops × O(log n) = O(n log n), worst case too
Not stable. The in-place version uses a max-heap
and parks each popped maximum at the end.
